This event is for everyone, from children in strollers to seniors nearing 100 years old. That’s how we can make the most of the day.

name: MartinCrossen Trail Run

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Barneløpet for 3–5 år og paraklassen på 500 meter er gratis, og krever ingen påmelding på forhånd.

description: MartinCrossen Trail Run 2026 is a trail race starting and finishing at Voksenjordet in Sørkedalen, Oslo. The race makes its world premiere on November 4, 2026, and is inspired by the ski race Martincrossen and Martin Johnsrud Sundby, who will also take part as a commentator. The race offers a unique atmosphere with pyrotechnics, flames, lights and music. It is held in the evening in November, making the darkness and use of headlamps an important part of the experience. The event is inclusive, with categories for children, youth, para athletes, recreational runners and competitive runners.
course_highlights: Trail running on challenging technical terrain, with an easy start and a tough finish
Evening race; headlamps are used on the 3 km and 8 km distances
A unique atmosphere with pyrotechnics, flames, lights and music
additional: The children's race for ages 3–5 and the 500 m para race are free and require no registration. A companion for para athletes is free; contact mari@roail.no. All participants receive medals. Kokkeløren will provide food. Late registration opens on November 2 at 12:00, with an increased price and a limited number of race bibs. Start times vary from 17:30 to 18:00 for the different categories. Register via EQ-timing. The children's race for ages 3–5 and the 500 m para category are free. Parking is available at Bogstad School and Bogstad Golf Club; bus 42 stops at the start area. A kiosk is available.

name: Begbyjoggen
description: Begbyjoggen is a weekly recreational run in Fredrikstad, offering an accessible event for everyone. The race takes place on gravel paths in the lit trail network. The main course is 6.8 km, starting at the Begbyporten clubhouse and passing Bjørneklova, heading down Alleen, going around the golf course, and returning via Bjørneklova. There is also a separate 4.6 km course for those who want to walk or jog. The event takes place every Wednesday at 18:00, and tickets are sold through Strava.com.
course_highlights: 6.8 km course on gravel paths in the lit trail network
Start and finish at the Begbyporten clubhouse
Separate 4.6 km course for walkers and joggers
additional: Weekly recreational run every Wednesday at 18:00. An accessible event for everyone. Tickets are sold through Strava.com. The course follows gravel paths in the lit trail network. Start and finish at the Begbyporten clubhouse. The weekly gathering is listed as Wednesdays at 18:00 at Begbyporten (the “clubhouse”).

name: Nightrun Oslo

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Fra 7. oktober – 100 kr rabatt til og med 20. oktober

description: Ledlenser Nightrun Oslo is an exciting night race held at the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences at Sognsvann. The race offers an atmospheric experience, with headlamps illuminating the trail and reflectors along the course helping participants find their way in the dark. There are separate men’s and women’s categories across several age groups, and all participants receive a medal and the chance to win great prize-draw prizes. The event has a social atmosphere, with self-service bag storage and race-bib collection before the race.
course_highlights: The race follows trails at the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences at Sognsvann
Headlamps illuminate the course in the dark
Reflectors along the course provide visibility and safety
additional: Ledlenser will provide a limited number of headlamps for testing and borrowing during the race, on a first-come, first-served basis. There is self-service bag storage in the start area, and the baggage tag from the race bib must be attached to the bag. There are separate men’s and women’s categories for under 25, 25–39, 40–54, and over 55 years. The top three men and women overall will receive prizes. A headlamp is mandatory; a limited number of lamps can be borrowed. All participants receive a medal. Race-bib collection takes place at Löplabbet Oslo, Pilestredet 7, November 2–4, from 10:00 to 19:00, and at the start venue from 16:00 on race day. There is self-service bag storage.

name: Ledlenser Nightrun Oslo

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Fra 7. oktober – 100 kr rabatt til og med 20. oktober

description: Ledlenser Nightrun Oslo is a unique trail race held on dark forest paths near the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences at Sognsvann. All participants run with headlamps, making for an exciting and atmospheric experience in the night-time darkness. There are separate men’s and women’s categories in different age groups, and everyone receives a medal and has the chance to win draw prizes. The race starts at 18:00, and self-service bag storage is available in the start area.
course_highlights: Trail race on dark forest paths at Sognsvann
Running with headlamps and reflective markings along the course
Separate men’s and women’s categories across several age groups
additional: Ledlenser provides a limited number of headlamps for testing and loan during the race on a first-come, first-served basis. Self-service bag storage is available in the start area; the bag tag from your race bib must be attached to your bag. Prizes are awarded to the top three men and women overall. Corporate registration is available, with the option of a dedicated stand and printing on shirts/race bibs. Race bibs can be collected at Löplabbet Oslo, Pilestredet 7, 2–4 November, 10:00–19:00, and at the start venue from 16:00 on race day. Self-service bag storage is available in the start area. There are separate men’s and women’s categories for the age groups under 25, 25–39, 40–54, and over 55. A limited number of headlamps from Ledlenser are available to borrow or test.

name: Samnanger Vinterkarusell - 1. løp
description: Samnanger Winter Series is an inclusive running series organised by Samnanger IL Running Group, suitable for all ages and ability levels. The races take place at Nesodden, with a choice of 2 km or 5 km distances. The Winter Series is held roughly every other Friday throughout the winter and focuses on competition, training and socialising. The race is free and open to everyone, with an emphasis on the joy of running and community in a safe environment.
course_highlights: The race takes place at Nesodden, with the start and finish in the same place
Choose between 2 km and 5 km distances; the 5 km course has been officially measured by NFIF
The races take place in the winter darkness, so reflective vests are recommended
additional: The running group is free, open to everyone and suitable for all ability levels. Races are held roughly every other Friday at 18:30. Reflective vests are recommended because of the dark winter conditions. Samnanger IL Running Group also offers group training every Monday at 18:10 in Hagabotnane. Races are held roughly every other Friday from November to March. Remember to wear a reflective vest.

name: Torsdagsløpet
description: The Thursday run in Sarpsborg was a real Easter treat on Maundy Thursday, with glorious weather and a well-deserved break from the long-forecast rain. The run, which takes place on Thursdays until mid-October, offers lovely routes through the extensive network of trails in Kalnesskogen. Although there were a few icy sections, conditions were generally excellent for both runners and organizers.

description: Barfrostløpet on 7 November 2026 offers three distances: 1,500 m, 5,000 m and 10,000 m, as well as a 4.3 km fun run, Run4Fun. The start and finish for all distances are outside Tanabru kindergarten, opposite the health centre, on marked, paved routes in central Tanabru. Age limits apply to the different competition classes, with participants ranging from 4 to 85 years old. Changing rooms will be open at Tana multipurpose hall. Food will be served, and there will be a season-opening chat after the race at Tanabru school, near the multipurpose hall.

description: 3-Sjøersløpet is one of Norway’s most enjoyable events to take part in, and takes place in Stavanger with 5,200 participants. The course is varied and beautiful, offering a great sightseeing experience of some of the best Stavanger has to offer. Follow one of our skilled pacers, who will help you maintain the right pace along the way, and experience the excitement of the crowds, flags, and music along the course.

description: Ålesund Winter Series consists of 5 races throughout the winter, starting at 14:00 from BestDrive in Fremmerholen every other Saturday from November to March. The first race in the 2025/2026 Winter Series takes place on Saturday, 8 November 2025. Participants can choose between two distances, 5 and 10 km, on accurately measured courses heading inland through Brusdalen. The 5 km distance also has a non-timed recreational class, and there is little car traffic on Gamle Brusdals veg.

description: Magni Marathon is an exciting race that attracts runners from all over the country. The course is varied, with both flat stretches and challenging hills, offering a great experience for beginners and experienced runners alike. The beautiful scenery around the race also adds an extra dimension to the event.

name: Morothon
description: Morothon is a traditional trail race held annually in Søgne, and it has become an important event for both local and visiting runners. The race is known for its challenging courses and the great atmosphere among participants. Today, Morothon offers several distances, including Langmoro at 20 km, Kortmoro at 10 km, and a children’s race. The most important thing about Morothon is taking part; it is a celebration of community, endurance, and joy.

name: 3-Sjøersløpet 2026

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Halv pris for de som er 15-24 år (født 2002-2011)

description: 3-Sjøersløpet is a popular half marathon held in Stavanger in November. The race offers a varied and scenic course that goes around three lakes, with approximately 80% of the distance on runnable gravel and the rest on asphalt. Participants enjoy a great atmosphere, with plenty of spectators, music and pacers to help runners maintain the right pace. The start and finish are at Forum Expo in Tjensvoll, and the race is suitable for both experienced runners and recreational runners looking for an enjoyable race in beautiful surroundings.
course_highlights: Approximately 80% of the course is on runnable gravel, with the rest on asphalt
The course goes around three lakes, with varied terrain and several hills
Several aid stations and toilets along the way, as well as strong spectator support
additional: The race starts in 12 waves, with 3–4 minutes between them. Pacers run at five-minute intervals from 1:20 to 2:30 (and 2:45). The start and finish are at Forum Expo, which also has changing rooms, baggage storage and toilets. After finishing, participants receive a medal, a banana, water and lapskaus. It is possible to transfer a race bib to another participant within the age groups. Parking is limited; arriving on foot, by bicycle or by bus is recommended. The start and finish are in Tjensvoll, approximately 3 km from Stavanger city centre. Participants must be at least 15 years old; the 15–24 age group pays half price. The Forum Expo exhibition hall is used before and after the race.

name: Fagerstrand Backyard Ultra Maraton
description: Fagerstrand Backyard Ultra Marathon 2026 is organized by Fagerstrand IF at Myklerud, Fagerstrand. This unique race starts on Saturday, November 7 at 09:00 and follows a simple but demanding format: a new 6.7 km lap starts every hour. The race continues on a “last man standing” basis until only one runner remains, or is decided on lap 12 if several runners are still competing. Participants can choose their strategy: run fast for a longer break or take it easier to conserve energy. There will be a banquet for runners and their companions.
course_highlights: 6.7 km laps every hour
Last man standing format
Decided on lap 12 if several runners are still competing
additional: Doors open at 08:00. There will be a banquet for runners and their +1; banquet tickets are sold separately. A service fee of NOK 15 per ticket is added at checkout (maximum NOK 30 per order). Race starts at 09:00, with doors opening at 08:00. Limited number of tickets. Banquet ticket sold separately.

description: Grimstadvatnet Rundt is a 7.8 km road race run mainly on asphalt, with a relatively flat course. The race is part of the Hareid Winter Series, which consists of four races held on the first Saturday in November, December, January and February. The first race in the series was held in 1981, and awards are presented after the fourth and final race in February. To qualify for an award, runners must complete at least three of the four races. Scores are based on the three best races, with bonus points for completing all four.
course_highlights: 7.8 km road race, mainly on asphalt
Relatively flat course
Part of the Hareid Winter Series, with four races
additional: Registration takes place at Hareid clubhouse from 13:00 on race day. Changing facilities are available at the clubhouse. A one-time Norwegian Athletics Federation licence is required for races outside a track if you do not have an annual licence. The race starts at 14:00 at Hareid clubhouse, with registration from 13:00. The series consists of four races, and an award requires participation in at least three.

name: Barfrostløpet 2026
location: Tanabru barnehage, Tana bru, Tana, Norway
description: Barfrostløpet 2026 takes place in Tanabru, with the start and finish outside Tanabru kindergarten. The race offers three distances: 1,500 metres, 5,000 metres and 10,000 metres. The 10 km race consists of two laps. The courses follow marked, established routes in central Tanabru. The event includes changing facilities at Tana multi-purpose hall, as well as food and a season-opening chat at Cafè Kievra after the race. Results will be published at sirbma.no and can be followed live via EQtiming.
course_highlights: Three distances: 1,500 m, 5,000 m and 10,000 m
Start and finish outside Tanabru kindergarten in the town centre
Marked, established routes in central Tanabru; course maps are available
additional: Changing facilities are open at Tana multi-purpose hall. Food and a season-opening chat for all participants are included in the entry fee and take place at Cafè Kievra after the race. The address for bib and timing-chip collection is Ringveien 55, 9845 Tana. Results will be announced at sirbma.no and can be followed live on EQtiming. Mass start at 12:00. Changing facilities are available at Tana multi-purpose hall, and food after the race is included in the entry fee. The start and finish are at Tanabru kindergarten.

description: Lierløpet is one of Norway’s fastest courses. The race takes place on a wide path that is popular with runners and recreational athletes in the Drammen area. It offers 5K, 10K, and half-marathon distances, making it accessible to both experienced runners and beginners.

name: Refleksløpet Arendal, Fossbekk
description: Welcome to the Refleksløpet in Arendal, an atmospheric race in the dark held at Fossbekk in Arendal. The race offers two distances: a short 4.8 km course and a long 7.8 km course, as well as the option to walk without timing. The race starts early in the evening, and participants are encouraged to wear a headlamp for a safe and magical experience. This is a social event where friends, family and running buddies can get together for a fun and active evening.
course_highlights: Two distances: a 4.8 km short course and a 7.8 km long course
The race takes place in the dark, so a headlamp is recommended
Start at the Fossbekk parking area, a scenic location between Krøgenes and Longum
additional: The race office opens at 16:30 for registration and bib collection. The long course starts at 18:00, the short course at 18:05, and walkers without timing can start at 17:00. The first 30 people to register will have the chance to win a Mizuno bag. Registering before race day is recommended to avoid stress. Participants receive a 15% discount on headlamps at Brekke sport's physical store. The long course starts at 18:00 and the short course at 18:05. Walkers without timing can start at 17:00. The race office opens at 16:30, and a headlamp is recommended.

name: Refleksløpet Kristiansand
description: The Reflective Run in Kristiansand invites you to a magical evening run with headlamps on Thursday, November 13. The start and finish are at Fant Olsen in Baneheia, with registration opening at 16:30. Participants can start from 17:00, while the mass start with timing is at 18:00. The course is 4.1 km long and follows the outer edge of Baneheia, marked with reflective markers. Participants must bring a headlamp, and mulled juice and porridge will be served after the finish.

description: Refleksløpet in Kristiansand is a 4.1 km evening race held in Baneheia, starting and finishing at Fant Olsen. The race takes place in the dark and is marked with reflective markers, creating a unique autumn experience. Participants are encouraged to bring a light to get the most out of the race. After the finish, gløgg and porridge are served, and there is a prize drawing based on race numbers.
course_highlights: 4.1 km evening race in Baneheia
The course is marked with reflective markers
Start and finish at Fant Olsen

Member discount code: 26 ABIK (membership will be checked). After the finish, gløgg and porridge are served, and there is a prize drawing based on race numbers. A light is required. Untimed start from 17:00 and mass start with timing at 18:00; the event office opens at 16:30. Gløgg and porridge are served after the finish, and there will be a prize drawing.

description: Welcome to Kristiansund Backyard Ultra, a unique endurance race taking place on Saturday, November 15, starting at Frei School. Participants must complete a 6.7 km loop every hour on the hour, and the race continues for 12 hours. If you cannot finish the loop within the hour or do not start the next loop, you are out of the race. This format tests both physical endurance and mental strength, pushing runners to complete “just one more loop.” Everyone who completes at least one loop receives a medal.

The race is suitable for anyone looking for an active and social experience in November.

The event runs from November 7 to 8, 2026

organizer: Lørenskog Friidrettsklubb (Sørum IL er teknisk arrangør)
description: Vinterkarusellen på Romerike is a running series organized by Lørenskog Friidrettslag, offering races for different age groups, from children to veterans. The races take place during the winter months and provide a great opportunity for both recreational and competitive runners to compete and stay in shape. The event has a long tradition and includes several distances and classes suited to different levels. Participants aged 13 to 80 must have an athletics license, which also serves as insurance.
course_highlights: Certified 5 km on the Bingenrunden
Asphalt loop course starting at Sørum school
Previous race reports describe the course as flat and suitable for fast times in good conditions
additional: Participants aged 13 to 80 must purchase an athletics license individually. Children under 13 are covered by the children's sports insurance and do not need their own license. Previous editions have offered online registration and race-day registration. Participants aged 13–80 must have an athletics license; children under 13 are covered by the children's sports insurance.

name: BlåmansLøpene - Etappe 3
description: Blåmansløpene 2026 consists of three spectacular races from Fjellveien to Blåmanen, with the start and finish at the same location, but on different routes featuring trails, nearby mountains and varied running challenges. Stage 3, held on 14 November, follows a demanding, technical course on trails towards Blåmanen, finishing at Tindevann. The race is suited to runners who enjoy challenging terrain and technical sections, and trail shoes are recommended. Varegg IL welcomes everyone to a great running experience in beautiful surroundings in Bergen.
course_highlights: Start at Fjellveien by «Damen» and finish at Tindevann
Technically challenging trails up Blåmanen through varied terrain
The course includes trails such as Permisjonstien, Sandviksbatteriet, Rundemanen and Blåmansveien
additional: Trail shoes are recommended for the technical sections. The course includes challenging climbs and technical trails. The start and finish are at the same location for all three races. Entry fees are paid by bank transfer or VIPPS to Varegg Fleridrett. The organizer recommends trail shoes; the course is technical, and runners accustomed to trail terrain may have an advantage.

description: Sognefjord Backyard is a unique backyard ultra race held in Sogndal on Saturday, 14 November 2026, starting at 08:00 from Meieriet. The race consists of a 6.7 km loop with approximately 45 metres of elevation gain, run every hour on the hour. Participants have one hour to complete each loop. The competition continues until only one participant remains who has completed one more loop than everyone else. This race challenges both endurance and mental strength, and is suited to runners who want to test themselves in a unique format with no fixed distance.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loop with approximately 45 metres of elevation gain
Start and finish at Meieriet in Sogndal
The course follows pavements and shared pedestrian and cycle paths, in both daylight and darkness
additional: Maximum 100 participants. Minimum age: 18. Start and finish at Meieriet, which also serves as a base with space for drop bags and rest. The café at Meieriet is open for food and drink purchases, but participants must arrange their own provisions. Assistance and provisions are only permitted in the start and finish area. Each participant may have one dedicated support person in the participant area. Registration is binding and non-refundable, but the entry can be transferred to another person via Racetracker. Warnings are given 3 and 1 minute before each start. One winner is declared: the participant who completes one more loop than everyone else; otherwise, there is no winner. Start at Meieriet in Sogndal at 08:00 on Saturday, 14 November 2026. If you cannot complete the loop within the hour, you are out of the race.

name: Fakkeltoget Løvstakken
description: The Løvstakken Torchlight Procession is an enjoyable mountain hike for all ages, held every year in support of the Norwegian Cancer Society. No particular level of fitness is required, and you’re welcome to come without children. The hike up Løvstakken begins as darkness falls and the city lights become visible. At the summit, there’s a medal ceremony, a barbecue and other fun activities, before everyone lights their torches for the group hike back down. Pizza, mulled wine and gingerbread are served at the finish.

This race, taking place on Saturday, August 23, 2025, is not for the faint-hearted, as it features 37 km of technically demanding terrain and nearly 1,000 metres of elevation gain. Participants will experience trails that cross rough, rocky ground, and after many hours of preparation, they will feel ready for this challenge.

name: Hodelyktløpet Østmarka
description: Østmarka Trail Challenge – The Headlamp Race is a technically demanding trail race of approximately 12 km, running mainly on blue- and red-marked trails in Østmarka. The route will be marked all the way by the organizers, but there is definitely a chance of taking a wrong turn, so it is important to pay close attention, especially at trail junctions. A good headlamp is essential! From the start at Skullerud, we follow the Flyktningeruta up to Rundvann, before taking the technically challenging blue trail downhill.

description: The Headlamp Run in Østmarka is a technically demanding trail race of approximately 12 km, mainly following blue- and red-marked trails in Østmarka. The race takes place in the evening, starting at 19:30, and a good headlamp is required to navigate in the dark. Runners face challenging terrain with 400 metres of elevation gain. The race offers a nature experience in beautiful surroundings, with demanding trails. There are no food or drink stations along the route, so runners must bring their own drinks.

The event attracts both experienced ultrarunners and beginners who want to test their limits in a supportive and motivating environment. The race is sold out, and prizes include a large achievement medal for those who reach 150 km (men) and 130 km (women).

name: Klubbmesterskap 5k
description: The Club Championship 5K is a running competition that is part of Tjøme Running Club’s events. The courses are officially measured, and the race is run over a distance of 5 km. This championship gives members the opportunity to compete for club championship titles and set club records. The race takes place at the beautiful Grønneset by Ånøya on Wednesday, June 25, with the start from 18:00, and is designed to challenge both beginners and experienced runners.

name: Bergen Cider Marathon
description: Bergen Cider Marathon is a unique race combining running, Bergen and cider for a different kind of marathon experience. The course goes through Fyllingsdalstunnelen, the world’s longest tunnel for pedestrians and cyclists, and continues through beautiful surroundings in Bergen. Half-marathon runners complete one lap, while marathon runners complete two laps and pass through the tunnel four times. After the race, participants are invited to a cider party featuring tastings of different ciders and food inspired by Bergen and Hardanger.
course_highlights: The course goes through Fyllingsdalstunnelen, the world’s longest tunnel for pedestrians and cyclists
Three laps around Store Lungegårdsvannet in central Bergen
A measured course through beautiful surroundings in Bergen
additional: All participants receive a technical running shirt included in the price. There will be no medal, but a certificate can be printed after the race. Refreshments during the race are non-alcoholic, with non-alcoholic cider, water and squash/energy drink. After the race, a separate cider party will be held at Siderbaren, with tastings of at least seven different ciders and food. It requires a separate ticket and has limited capacity. Registration is for the selected distance, and it is possible to transfer your entry to someone else. Start at 09:00. A technical running shirt is included. Aid stations serve non-alcoholic cider, water and squash or energy drink. The cider party at Siderbaren requires separate registration and has limited capacity. Age limit: 18 years.

description: Karmøy Marathon wraps up the running season in the fresh West Norwegian air. The marathon course takes you through three towns, along the coastline on both the east and west sides of Karmøy, with the North Sea as your closest neighbour. This year, IL Trio is strongly represented, with participants in both the full and half marathon, including Emil Solli Stafsnes, who is taking part in his first full marathon. Results will be posted on Trio’s Facebook page as they become available.

name: Borredalen Rundt – Juleløpet
description: Borredalen Rundt is the Fredrikstad district’s most longstanding recreational race, held since 1962. The race takes place on Tuesday evenings during the April-to-October season. Its approximately 5.5 km course winds around Borredalsdammen through scenic surroundings, along forest trails, rocky terrain and sandy paths. This is an informal weekly event with no entry fee, built on volunteer effort and a sense of community among women and men who enjoy running. Participants register at the start and set off together, keeping their own time.
course_highlights: The course follows forest trails, rocky terrain and sandy paths around Borredalsdammen

Scenic surroundings in the Fredrikstad forest
additional: The race is held every Tuesday during the summer season, with a mass start. Volunteers run the event, with a six-week rotation in the race office. The Borredalen Rundt tradition began in 1962.

description: Lierløpet is an exciting race series offering different distances for both men and women of all ages. Participants can choose between 5 km, 10 km, and 21.1 km, with age categories for everyone aged 11 and up. The race takes place in scenic surroundings and follows the well-known Linnesrunden, an easy-to-run route suitable for everyone. Prizes are awarded to the top runners, and there are opportunities to set personal records.

additional: Participants aged 13 to 80 must purchase an athletics license individually. Children under 13 are covered by the child sports insurance and do not need their own license. Lørenskog Friidrettslag has training groups for different age groups and ability levels, and organizes several running and athletics events in the area. Participants aged 13 to 80 must have an athletics license; children under 13 are covered by the Child Sports Insurance.

description: The Bergen Marathon Series is a series of six races throughout the year, where participants can run both the half marathon and the full marathon. Bergen is regarded as Norway’s number one marathon city, and the series places great emphasis on quality and runners’ enjoyment, even though the races offer tough challenges. By completing five of the six races in the series, you receive a commemorative plaque. The February Marathon is the second race in the series and is held during the winter months, offering a great opportunity to test your fitness early in the year.
course_highlights: The races are held in Bergen, known as Norway’s number one marathon city
The series consists of six races, with both half-marathon and full-marathon options
The courses are quality-assured with a national course certificate and an IAU label
additional: Kondis membership gives a NOK 50 discount. You can provide an annual licence from the Norwegian Athletics Federation to avoid paying for a one-time licence. The minimum age for the marathon is 18. The Bergen Marathon Series is held in collaboration with BFG Bergen Running Club. It is possible to rent a function room at Fana Stadium. Complete five of the Bergen Marathon Series races to receive a plaque. Details about registration and the 2027 edition are not provided in the sources.

name: Bjørgene løpskarusell - 6. løp
description: Bjørgene Running Series is a long-standing race series organized by the athletics group of Torvastad Sports Club. The 2026/2027 season will be the 19th in the series, with races held on the first Tuesday of each month from October to March. The races take place in Bjørgene, Karmøy, and attract many runners of all ages. The event offers a friendly, inclusive atmosphere, with light refreshments after the finish.
course_highlights: Run through scenic surroundings in Bjørgene, Karmøy
Races are held on the first Tuesday of each month from October to March
Start at 19:00; race bibs can be collected from 18:00
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 18:00. Juice, biscuits and fruit are served after the finish. The running series is organized by the athletics group of Torvastad Sports Club and relies on volunteer efforts.

name: Samnanger Vinterkarusell - 5. løp
description: Samnanger IL Running Group invites you to Vinterkarusellen, a friendly and sociable race starting and finishing at Nesodden. You can choose between 2 km and 5 km, with the 5 km course officially measured by NFIF. The race is suitable for all levels and paces, whether you want to compete, set a new personal best, maintain your fitness or simply enjoy a sociable run. Remember to wear reflective gear, as it is dark at this time of year.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Nesodden
Choice of 2 km or 5 km distances
The 5 km course is officially measured by the Norwegian Athletics Federation (NFIF)
additional: The race is held approximately every other Friday throughout the winter. It is a free, accessible event suitable for everyone. The running group focuses on the joy of running and community. Wearing a reflective vest is recommended because of the dark winter season. Start at 18:30. The organizer reminds participants to wear reflective gear in the dark.

name: Snøkuten - Kaashagarunden
description: Snøkuten Kaashagarunden is a 6.9-kilometer cross-country race organized by Veldre Friidrett, marking the start of the 42nd season of the Vinterkarusellen Snøkuten. The race takes place in Ringsaker, Hedmark, and attracts around 100 participants despite varying weather conditions. Participants must wear a reflective vest and take care in traffic. Both timed and fitness classes are offered. The event is especially important this year, with many opportunities for exercise and competition having been cancelled.
course_highlights: Cross-country race in Ringsaker, Hedmark
Distance of 6.9 kilometers
Reflective vest required; participants must take care in traffic
additional: Both timed and untimed fitness classes are available. The event attracts around 100 participants each time. The race marks the start of the 42nd season of the Vinterkarusellen Snøkuten. A reflective vest is required; a headlamp and good winter footwear may be useful.

name: Frikarusellen - 6. løp
location: Espeland Idrettsplass, Espeland, Arna, Bergen, Norway
description: The Frikarusellen is a winter running series organized by Idrettslaget Fri in Arna, Bergen. The races take place on a certified 5 km course that starts at Espeland sports ground and runs via Gamle Haukeland station, mainly on walking and cycling paths with little traffic. The series consists of six races throughout the winter and is suitable for both young people and adults, with a friendly atmosphere and a shared love of running. IL Fri has a long tradition as an organizer and also offers discounts for club members.
course_highlights: Certified 5 km course between Espeland and Gamle Haukeland station
The course runs mostly on walking and cycling paths or roads with little traffic
Start and finish at Espeland sports ground
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Espelandshallen on race day between 18:00 and 18:55. Registration is open until 18:55 on race day. A license fee applies in addition for participants over 13 without an annual license. A fee of NOK 50 applies for forgotten race numbers for those registered for all races. Results are published at www.eqtiming.no. Race-number distribution and changing facilities are available from 18:00.

name: Landeveisløp 8km
location: IL Skade Clubhouse, Kåsa, Nome, Telemark, Norway
description: The Lunde Road Race is a traditional 8 km road race organised by IL Skade’s athletics group. It follows the beautiful, flat route alongside the Telemark Canal, starting and finishing at IL Skade’s clubhouse at Kåsa. The race has a long history and has been held more than 50 times, previously as part of the Vinterkarusellen in Telemark. After the race, participants are invited to socialise over cordial, coffee and waffles, followed by an informal prize-giving at the clubhouse, where changing rooms and showers are also available.
course_highlights: Flat route of approximately 7.8 km alongside the Telemark Canal
Start and finish at IL Skade’s clubhouse at Kåsa
More than 50 years of tradition; one of the oldest races in the area
additional: Registration is available on race day at the clubhouse from approximately 11:00 to 12:30, or by SMS to Sveinung Håland (98 62 38 62). Changing rooms and showers are available at the clubhouse. After the race, participants can socialise over cordial, coffee and waffles, followed by an informal prize-giving. Registration on race day is at the clubhouse from approximately 11:00 to 12:30, or by SMS.

name: Vinterkarusellen i Ålesund - 5. løp
description: Ålesund Winter Series is a long-standing race series held over five races during the winter months in Ålesund. The races take place on officially measured courses in Brusdalen, over distances of 5 and 10 km, and start at BestDrive in Fremmerholen. The courses are relatively flat and follow Gamle Brusdals veg, with little traffic on race days. After the race, juice, cola, cake and coffee are served, and medals are awarded to those who take part in three or more races in the series.
course_highlights: Officially measured 5 and 10 km courses in Brusdalen
Relatively flat courses with little traffic on Gamle Brusdals veg
Start and finish at BestDrive in Fremmerholen
additional: The races start at 13:00 for the 10 km and 13:05 for the 5 km. There is a non-timed recreational category over 5 km. Gift prizes are drawn after each race. Medals are awarded to participants who complete three or more races in the series. Juice, cola, cake and coffee are served in the finish area after the race. Registration is through EQ Timing. The 5 km is also available as a non-timed recreational category. Juice, cola, cake and coffee are served in the finish area.

name: Hamarkarusellen vinter Løp 6
description: The Hamarkarusellen Winter Series is a running series for everyone, whether you are an experienced runner, a recreational runner, or simply looking to get outside for some fresh air. The series consists of six races over the winter months, all on the same 5 km course, starting and finishing at Prestrudhallen in Hamar. The races focus on activity, achievement, and socializing, and everyone is welcome regardless of pace—you can run, jog, walk, or combine them. Participants who take part in at least four of the six races receive a finisher’s prize. The event offers a friendly atmosphere, with gingerbread and cordial at the finish.
course_highlights: Six races on the same 5 km course, starting and finishing at Prestrudhallen in Hamar
The course is suitable for running, jogging, and walking
A social and motivating winter series focused on achievement and activity
additional: A finisher’s prize is awarded to everyone who takes part in at least four of the six races. Participants are encouraged to wear a Santa hat, and gingerbread and cordial are served at the finish. The member price applies to members of corporate sports clubs and individual members of the Innlandet Regional Corporate Sports Association. Everyone is welcome, with an accessible format and room for all levels. Registration is available for individual races or the entire series.

name: Åsane løpskarusell 2027 | Løp 4
description: Åsane running series is a recreational running series with weekly 5 km races in Åsane, Bergen, starting and finishing at IKEA. The course is nationally certified, suits all levels, and is led by experienced coaches. The series has a social and inclusive atmosphere and also offers training sessions for those who would like to join the running group. Race numbers are collected on site before the races, and family and individual registration are available.
course_highlights: 5 km course, measured and nationally certified
Start and finish inside IKEA, at the rear facing south
The course was measured and certified by Ivar Andreas Sandø
additional: Race numbers are collected in the IKEA garage between 18:00 and 18:45. Race numbers must be worn visibly and must not be folded or damaged. A replacement race number costs 100 kr. The races take place on Thursdays. Start time: 19:00. Race numbers can be collected in the IKEA garage between 18:00 and 18:45. The start and finish are at the rear of the IKEA building, facing south.

name: Frozen Lake Marathon
description: Frozen Lake Marathon is a unique running event held on the frozen surface of Lake Tisleifjorden in Norway, 819 meters above sea level. Participants run entirely on ice, on a course with the flattest elevation profile in the world, making it an unforgettable experience. The race is limited to 500 participants and offers both a half marathon and a full marathon. The entry includes an official long-sleeved race shirt and a medal for all finishers, with warm soup and bread served after the race. The course is carefully monitored and laid out just days before the race to ensure safety on the ice.
course_highlights: 100% ice surface on Lake Tisleifjorden, with ice about 80 cm thick
The flattest elevation profile in the world
Energy stations at several points, offering sports drinks, water, energy bars, dried fruit, and chocolate
additional: Limited to 500 participants. Transfer is included only for participants staying at Oset Fjellhotell; shuttle service is available at a cost from Storefjell Resort. Parking near the race area is very limited; studded tires are recommended for driving. Bag-drop service is available with a bib tag. Basic changing tents and portaloo toilets are provided. Warm soup with bread is served after the race. Arrival by train to Gol is recommended; the official race hotel is Oset Fjellhotell. The entry includes an official long-sleeved race shirt and a medal, and warm soup with bread is served after the race. Transport is included for participants staying at Oset Fjellhotell; parking near the race area is very limited.

name: 6. Ekeberg Backyard Ultra
description: Ekeberg Backyard Ultra is a classic backyard ultra race held in Oslo’s “central park” at Ekeberg. The race takes place during the dark and cold time of year, giving participants the opportunity to run together with the ultra-running family in beautiful surroundings, with views of Oslo’s skyline and the Oslofjord. The event offers a unique atmosphere with live music, good vibes and facilities such as changing rooms and tents. A maximum of 110 participants can take part, and everyone who completes at least one lap receives a medal.
course_highlights: Run through beautiful scenery with views of the Oslofjord and Oslo’s skyline
The event takes place at Bekkelagshøgda Tennis Club, with access to changing rooms and tents
Live music and good vibes with the ultra-running family
additional: Participants receive a race bib and tracker for automatic live recording of lap times. Drinks, snacks and some hot food are provided. Maximum 110 participants. Everyone who completes at least one lap receives a medal. The race starts at 09:00. Registration opens on 1 December 2026 at 00:01. Participants receive a tracker for lap times, access to the venue and changing rooms, drinks, snacks and hot food. Medals are awarded to everyone who completes at least one lap.

name: Lillestrøms Høyeste Trappeløp
description: Lillestrøm’s Highest Stair Race takes place at Scandic Lillestrøm, with its 12 floors, and offers a real challenge for anyone who wants to test themselves, their friends, family, or colleagues. The race is suitable for all levels and is open to participants aged 13 and over. The event starts at 18:00, with race bibs and timing chips available for collection from 17:00. EMIT timing chips record start time, split time, and finish time, and results are displayed in real time on a large screen on the 2nd floor.
course_highlights: The race goes up 12 floors at Scandic Lillestrøm
EMIT timing chips record start, split, and finish times
Results are displayed in real time on a large screen on the 2nd floor
additional: Race bibs and timing chips can be collected from 17:00. Warm-up is self-directed, outdoors or indoors where space is available. Luggage can be left in a hotel meeting room at your own risk. Toilets are on the 1st and 2nd floors. Using public transport is recommended, as Scandic Lillestrøm is 50 metres from the train station and 150 metres from the bus station. Parking is limited, but commuter parking in the parking garage or at Varemessen (approx. 200 m away) is recommended if arriving by car. Group registration and a single invoice are available for corporate sports clubs and businesses. Timing is done using EMIT chips.

name: Sandtangstafetten
description: Sandtangstafetten is a traditional relay held at Sandtangen in Bryne. The race has four legs on varied surfaces, including forest floor, gravel and grass, and offers both a short and a long course for different age groups, from age 7 to seniors. The event starts in the evening and lasts approximately one hour and fifteen minutes, with a focus on team spirit and a great atmosphere. It is a family-friendly race, with many mixed teams as well as all-girls and all-boys teams competing in different categories.
course_highlights: Short course for ages 7–10, with 110 m legs on forest floor, gravel and grass
Long course for ages 11 and older, with 370 m and 420 m legs on varied surfaces
Four legs per relay team, with changeovers at Sandtangen
additional: Start times for the different categories are from 18:00 to 18:36. Participants are advised to arrive 45 minutes before the start for a course and changeover briefing. Parking is available at Vianor Bryne (north) and Storstova (south). Registration is available via a link or by emailing pamelding@brynefriidrett.no. Parking at Vianor Bryne or Storstova.

description: GIF-Joggen Backyard Ultra takes place in Gressvikmarka, starting Saturday, April 3 at 08:00. The race consists of up to 12 laps on a 6.7 km course through varied and challenging terrain. Participants run one lap every hour and continue for as long as they can, aiming to complete as many laps as possible or all 12. All participants receive a medal, and those who complete every lap can log over 80 km in their training diary. Facilities include a heated shelter, toilets, changing rooms, and some fruit and baked goods.
course_highlights: A 6.7 km course through varied terrain
Up to 12 laps, with over 80 km for those who complete them all
The course is marked with red and white ribbons
additional: Check-in and registration from 07:00 on race day. To continue, participants must be ready for the next lap at the top of each hour. A heated shelter, toilets, and changing rooms are available. Bring a change of clothes, drinks, food, and possibly a headlamp. The course may be wet and muddy; a camping chair is recommended for the break area. The previous edition had a maximum of 77 participants. The race started at 08:00, and runners had to be ready at the start at the top of each hour to continue. A heated shelter, toilets, and changing rooms were available. Sources give conflicting information about the date in 2027.

name: Holmestrand maraton
description: Holmestrand Marathon is a friendly running event that has been a regular fixture on the race calendar since 2013. The race is held every year on the Saturday after Easter and offers beautiful, easy-to-run courses along the Holmestrand Fjord and through the city’s charming streets. Distances are available for all levels, from 5 km to the marathon, and the course has been officially measured and internationally approved by World Athletics. The event is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners, and also includes a free children’s race called Miniton.
course_highlights: Easy-to-run, personal-best-friendly 5 km loop course
Course along the Holmestrand Fjord and through the city streets
Officially measured and internationally approved by World Athletics
additional: All children can take part in the free Miniton children’s race. The race offers the option to run with or without a time. There are food and drink stations, prizes, and opportunities to follow the race along the course. The race is held every year on the Saturday after Easter. Distances: 5 km, 10 km, half marathon, marathon, and the free Miniton for children. For the 5 km, you can choose to run with or without a time. The event also offers the combinations marathon + 10 km and half marathon + 5 km.

description: Bergen Ultra is a challenging ultramarathon organized by Maratonkarusellen in collaboration with BFG Bergen Løpeklubb. The event offers distances of 63.3 km and 100 km, as well as a half marathon and marathon, and takes place at Fana Stadium in Bergen. Maratonkarusellen places great emphasis on quality and participant enjoyment, despite the event’s tough challenges. The minimum age is 18, and the race is part of a series of long-distance events held in both spring and autumn.
course_highlights: Ultramarathon distances of 63.3 km and 100 km
Organized in collaboration with BFG Bergen Løpeklubb
The races start and take place at Fana Stadium in Bergen
additional: Kondis members receive a NOK 50 discount. A year-round license from the Norwegian Athletics Federation can be provided by giving the license number, and a one-time license does not need to be paid for. Prices increase by NOK 50 two weeks before race day, by a further NOK 50 four days before, and the price on race day is NOK 650. The minimum age for the marathon is 18. The start and finish are at Fana Stadium. The half marathon is one lap, the marathon two laps, and the 63 km race three laps. The listed start times are 09:00 for 63 km, 10:00 for the marathon, and 11:00 for the half marathon. The prices and race details apply to the published 2026 edition; information for 3 April 2027 is not provided in the sources.

name: Solsiå sentrumsløp
description: Solsiå Sentrumsløp 2027 takes place in Sandnes city centre and features a circuit where participants choose how many laps to complete within six hours. There is also a separate children’s race of approximately 600 metres in Langgata. The race has an informal, inclusive character, focusing on local runners and safe preparation. Registration and payment are handled directly by the organiser, not through Førstart.
course_highlights: A 3 km circuit in Sandnes city centre
Choose how many laps to complete within six hours
A separate children’s race of approximately 600 metres in Langgata
additional: The children’s race starts at 11:30, and the circuit race starts at 12:00. Registration and payment are handled by the organiser, not through Førstart. Limited practical information about the race is available on Førstart. Feel free to invite others to the starting line. The circuit race starts at 12:00, and the children’s race starts at 11:30. Registration and payment are handled by the organiser.

name: Fredrikstadløpet
description: The Fredrikstadløpet is held in Gamlebyen in Fredrikstad, with the start and finish at Kongstenhallen. The event offers distances of 3 km for children and youth, 5 km, and a 21 km half marathon. All courses are on asphalt and are flat, with no elevation changes. The half-marathon course consists of three identical laps of approximately 7 km each, and the courses have been officially measured by a nationally approved course measurer. The event has international status and is a quality race, with course marshals at every intersection for safety.
course_highlights: Asphalt surface, except for a little gravel in the start and finish area
Flat courses with no elevation changes or sharp turns
The half marathon is run as three identical 7 km laps, with two pedestrian underpasses
additional: The start and finish area is behind Kongstenhallen. The children’s race is approximately 500 m and takes place near the start/finish area for the other distances. The course crosses busy roads in a few places, but course marshals are stationed at every intersection. Kondis members receive a discount on the entry fee. Registration for 2027 opens in September. The start and finish area, race office, and changing rooms are at Installatøren Arena, Torsnesveien 12, Gamle Fredrikstad. The course crosses busy roads in some places, with course marshals at the intersections.

description: Vårdilten is a traditional race held annually in Ålesund, formerly known as Teledilten. The race starts at Rattviksvingen in Gåseid and follows a 4.27 km route along sidewalks and gravel roads, including a challenging hill on the grounds of Sunnmøre Museum. Vårdilten is a popular spring event with both competitive and recreational categories, and prizes are awarded to the fastest man and woman after the race.
course_highlights: The route follows well-marked sidewalks and gravel roads
Includes a steep hill halfway through on the grounds of Sunnmøre Museum
Total distance of 4.27 km
additional: The race starts at Rattviksvingen in Gåseid, with ample parking at the start and across the road at Rema. After the race, trophies are awarded to the fastest man and woman, along with gift prizes. The race has a long tradition and has previously served as a local qualifier for the Holmenkollstafetten. Start: Wednesday, April 7, 2027, at 18:00. Registration through EQ Timing. Parking at the start and at Rema. Trophies for the fastest man and woman, as well as raffle prizes.

name: Tunnelløpet
organizer: BFG Bergen løpeklubb og Fyllingen Friidrett
description: Tunnelløpet is a fast 5 km road race that starts and finishes at the entrance to the tunnel on the Fyllingsdalen side in Bergen. The race runs partly on asphalt and partly on a royal-blue rubber surface inside the tunnel, providing stable, ideal running conditions without wind or rain, at a temperature of around 11–12 degrees year-round. The race is World Athletics-approved and attracts runners looking to set personal records. Children’s races are also held, with free entry and wave starts to ensure a good race experience for everyone.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the tunnel entrance on the Fyllingsdalen side
Run on asphalt on the way out and a royal-blue rubber surface on the way back through the tunnel
Stable conditions of around 11–12 degrees, with no wind or rain
additional: Wave starts are based on estimated finishing time, with around one minute between each wave. Children’s race distances are 400 metres for ages 3–5 and 1,500 metres for ages 6–10. Entry is free, but registration is mandatory. Race bibs are distributed the evening before the race at Oasen Senter. Race bib transfers are handled through Eq-timing for a fee. The main race has wave starts based on estimated finishing time. The children’s race is free but requires registration. Registration for the 2027 edition will open later in 2026.

description: Vestfold Running Series 2027 is a running series consisting of 8 races in the Tønsberg region, starting at 18:00, with two distances at each race. The series offers the joy of running, a sense of community and a great atmosphere for all levels, whether you want to set a personal best or simply be social and active. The races take place in beautiful surroundings, with electronic timing by EQ Timing. You can enter individual races or buy a season pass for all races at a discounted price.
course_highlights: Two distances at each race, ranging from approximately 2.3 km to 6.9 km depending on the location
Races in beautiful surroundings in the Tønsberg region, including Essoskogen, Tønsbergmarka, Vear, Teieskogen and Revetal
Start and finish at central locations such as the Sport1 store in Revetal, the Essoskogen car park and the playground at Teie school
additional: Season-pass participants collect their race number at the first race, while participants in individual races collect theirs from the race office 10 minutes before the start. Race numbers must be kept for the entire series. Electronic timing by EQ Timing. Course descriptions and profiles are available in the Facebook group and are sent out when registering for the season. Season registration and registration for individual races are available. Season-pass participants collect their race number at the first race and use it throughout the series; race numbers for individual races are collected and returned at each race.
